transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Yeah… I guess I came in because for the past few weeks I’ve had this really heavy, sad feeling, like a pressure just sitting on me most of the day. I’ll be at work, you know, smiling at patients and doing what I’m supposed to do—because you kind of have to in nursing, people are depending on you—and inside I feel like I’m barely keeping it together. It’s… it’s been hard to just feel normal.
Did this start after something stressful happened in your life?

I don’t know… I mean, nothing I can point to like, “that’s the thing that did it.” Work is always stressful, but it’s kind of always been like that, you know? Some weeks are worse than others, and there’s always some family thing or bill or someone needing something. But I can’t say there was one big event right before this started.
Before these past few weeks, had you been feeling down like this most days for a long time?

No… not for a long time. It’s more like… about three weeks now, I think. It started not too long after I found out I was pregnant, and I keep wondering if that’s connected somehow, or if I’m just overwhelmed—because everyone acts like you’re supposed to be excited, and then I feel guilty for not feeling that way all the time. But before that, no, I wasn’t feeling like this most days for months or anything.
Before this pregnancy, have you ever had another period in your life when you felt depressed like this for days at a time?

I’m not really sure… I mean, I’ve had bad days before, of course. Like after rough shifts or when family stuff piles up, I can get really worn down and emotional. Nursing school was stressful too—I remember crying in my car a few times before exams, which sounds dramatic, but it felt huge then.

But like this? I don’t know. I can’t think of another time where it felt the same. Maybe I’d have to think about it more.
Along with feeling down, have you been feeling especially anxious or on edge?

I don’t know… maybe a little? I mean, I wouldn’t say I’m panicking or anything. It’s hard to tell because everything feels kind of tense lately, but then also I keep thinking maybe that’s just normal life stuff. Like there’s always something to worry about, and I’ve always been the kind of person who makes lists in my head at night—my mom does that too, she’ll call me and start listing things she needs to do from like ten years ago.

So… I’m not sure if it’s “especially” anxious. Maybe on edge sometimes, but I don’t really know how to separate it from just feeling off.
Have you been less interested in, or gotten less pleasure from, the things you usually enjoy?

Yeah… I think so. I used to, after work, do something to kind of shake the day off—paint a little, or go to yoga, or sometimes salsa class if my friend dragged me. She’s one of those people who has, like, endless energy after a shift, which I never understood, but it used to help once I got there.

Lately I just… go home and sit on the couch. I see texts come in and I don’t answer them, even if they’re from people I like. It just all feels like too much effort, or like it won’t really feel good anyway, so I don’t bother.
How have you been sleeping lately?

I’m not sure how to answer that exactly. Sleep’s been kind of… inconsistent, I guess? Some nights I feel like I’m in bed forever just thinking, but then other nights I think I fall asleep okay. It’s hard to track.

My sister used to have this app that rated her sleep and she’d show me these charts like it was a school project, and I always thought, “I could never do that,” because I’d get too obsessed with whether I was doing it right. So I don’t really have, like, a clear number for you. It just doesn’t feel very restful lately, but I don’t know if that’s because of sleep itself or just everything else.
Before this pregnancy, was there ever a period of at least two weeks when you felt down most of the day nearly every day and lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

Before this pregnancy… I don’t know. I mean, I’ve had rough patches, definitely, like everyone does, especially with work being what it is. Nursing shifts kind of blur together sometimes, and then you get home and you’re too tired to remember if you were sad-sad or just exhausted.

Two weeks feels specific. I’m not sure I could point to a time and say yes, exactly that. I guess I’d need to think about it more.
Lately, have you been feeling guilty or like you’re letting people down?

I mean… I don’t know. “Letting people down” is such a broad thing, right? Like, at work you can always feel like you should’ve done one more thing, answered one more call light, checked in one more time. Nursing kind of trains you to think that way, I guess.

But lately specifically… I’m not sure I’d call it guilt, exactly. I haven’t really sat there thinking, “I’m a terrible person,” or anything like that. It’s more just… I don’t know, I notice when I’m not keeping up with people, and then I avoid thinking about it. Does that count?
At any time before this pregnancy, did you ever have a period of two weeks or longer when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

I’m still not totally sure. Like, I’ve had times where I felt really low, but whether it was most of the day nearly every day for two full weeks… I don’t know if I can say that clearly.

I’m bad with time frames, honestly. Everything before this pregnancy kind of gets sorted in my head by jobs or apartments or holidays, not by weeks. So I don’t want to say yes if I’m just guessing, but I also don’t want to say no like it never happened. I’d probably need to think about it more.
Before this pregnancy, had you ever gone through a time when you felt this same kind of depression?

I’m not sure I’d say it was the same. I’ve definitely been down before, but this feels… I don’t know, it’s hard to compare. Before I was pregnant, if I had a bad stretch, I could usually blame it on work or being tired or family stuff.

Like there was this one job where the schedule was awful, and I remember just coming home and kind of zoning out, but then nursing in general can do that to you. You eat cereal standing up at weird hours and think that’s normal.

So… I guess I don’t know. I can’t clearly say I had this same kind of depression before.
Have you noticed a change in your appetite lately?

Yeah… I think so. It’s not like I’m trying not to eat, exactly. I know I should be eating regularly, especially being pregnant, and I feel stupid even saying that because I’m a nurse, like I tell people this stuff all the time.

But most days food just sounds kind of… unappealing. Like nothing sounds good, and then I’ll get halfway through a clinic shift and realize I’ve basically only had coffee or some crackers. Or I’ll pack something and it just sits there. I don’t know, it’s been harder to make myself eat normally.
Have you been having more trouble concentrating lately?

Yeah… I think so. At work especially, which is kind of embarrassing to admit. I’ll read a medication order and then realize I didn’t actually take it in, so I reread it, sometimes more than once. Same with wound-care notes—stuff that usually is just routine for me.

It’s like my brain gets foggy, and then I start second-guessing things I normally wouldn’t even think twice about. Even small decisions can make me freeze for a minute, and then I get mad at myself because I know I know how to do this.
Lately, have you noticed yourself moving or speaking noticeably slower than usual, or feeling physically slowed down?

Yeah… I think that’s actually a good way to put it. Everything feels slowed down, like I’m moving through syrup or something.

Even at the clinic, little things that should be automatic—like gathering wound supplies or finishing charting—take me way longer than they should. And then I notice it and get irritated with myself, because it’s not like I don’t know what I’m doing. It just feels like my body and brain are both lagging.
Have you had any thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?

Yeah… um. That’s actually what kind of scared me enough to finally say something at my prenatal appointment.

I don’t— I haven’t made some plan to hurt myself or anything like that. It’s more like… I’ll be lying there and think, if I just didn’t wake up, that would be okay. Which sounds awful, especially with the baby, and then I feel terrible for even having the thought.

I almost didn’t bring it up because I kept thinking, “People have it worse,” and I’m supposed to know better, you know? But… yeah, those thoughts have been there.
